chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'How do I perform Tamattu'?' He said: 'Arrive at the time and say the Talbiyah for Hajj. When you enter Mecca, perform Tawaf around the House, pray two Rak'ahs behind the Maqam, run between Safa and Marwah, shorten your prayer, and release yourself from the Ihram restrictions of Umrah. You are not permitted to leave Mecca until you perform Hajj. The appropriate interpretation of these two narrations is to apply them to one who says the Talbiyah for Hajj and intends Umrah, because this is permissible during Taqiyyah. And if he mentions nothing at all, it is also permissible, and perhaps keeping it silent (Ismar) is better in some times.'

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: Taqiyyah (prudence or dissimulation in times of danger or political pressure)
key_terms.التَّمَتُّعُ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are performed separately with a break in between)
key_terms.الْإِضْمَارُ: Ismar (keeping the intention or declaration silent/internalized)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method for performing Hajj al-Tamattu' and how does Taqiyyah affect the verbal declaration?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar details the practical steps of Hajj al-Tamattu', emphasizing the transition from Umrah to Hajj while remaining in Mecca. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of Taqiyyah, explaining that the verbal Talbiyah can be internalized (Ismar) to avoid detection, making the internal intention sufficient and often preferable. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the validity of inner intent alongside outward ritual action.
